skill.name: segment-cdp
skill.description: Build Segment CDP integrations with browser and server tracking, typed tracking plans, identity resolution, destination controls, HTTP APIs, and data governance.

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by documented TypeScript examples, expected Segment API communication, normal environment configuration, and tracking-plan terminology. Two high-confidence semantic findings remain: the examples omit Stripe webhook verification and expose an unauthenticated edge tracking proxy that could permit forged analytics events.

remediation.issue: The Stripe webhook example processes request JSON without verifying the Stripe signature.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the webhook signature against the raw request body before parsing or processing any event, and reject invalid or replayed requests.

remediation.issue: The Cloudflare Worker example forwards untrusted request fields to Segment without authentication or validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require authentication, allowlist event names, validate payload schemas, limit field sizes, and add rate limiting before forwarding events.

semantic_findings.title: Stripe Webhook Verification Omitted
semantic_findings.description: The Stripe webhook example parses and processes request JSON without verifying a Stripe signature. A copied implementation could accept forged purchase and subscription events, corrupting customer profiles and analytics.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The complete webhook handler is shown, and no signature verification occurs before the body controls tracked events. The route is explicitly presented as a Stripe webhook example.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Analytics Proxy Example
semantic_findings.description: The Cloudflare Worker example accepts userId, action, and data from any request and forwards them to Segment without authentication, schema validation, or rate limiting. Attackers could forge events, poison analytics, or increase ingestion costs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handler directly destructures untrusted request JSON and passes every field to httpTrack. No access control or validation is present in the documented example.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent analytics events weaken reporting and customer profiles. This skill provides Segment patterns for browser, server, identity, routing, governance, and HTTP tracking.
actual_capabilities: Configure Analytics.js browser tracking in Next.js applications.
Implement batched server-side tracking with the Segment Node.js SDK.
Define typed event schemas and tracking plans for Segment Protocols.
Handle anonymous users, identification, aliases, and company groups.
Control event and PII routing across configured destinations.
Send identify, track, page, and batch calls through the Segment HTTP API.
limitations: Examples require adaptation, security review, and testing for each application.
The skill does not configure Segment workspaces or destinations automatically.
Consent management is discussed but not implemented in the sample flows.
Webhook and edge examples need authentication, validation, and abuse controls.

use_cases.title: Add Product Analytics
use_cases.description: Create consistent browser events, page views, and user identification for a Next.js product.

use_cases.title: Track Backend Revenue
use_cases.description: Design reliable server events for purchases, subscriptions, and webhook-driven activity.

use_cases.title: Govern Customer Data
use_cases.description: Define tracking plans, required properties, identity rules, and destination controls.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Segment Analytics.js event for [user action] with the properties [property list]. Use a static Object Action event name.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Tracking Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Segment tracking plan for [product area]. Include event names, descriptions, required properties, types, and naming rules.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Identity Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Segment identity flow for [application]. Cover anonymous activity, signup, login, logout reset, aliases, and organization groups.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Segment architecture: [details]. Assess consent, PII routing, schemas, retries, batching, webhook verification, endpoint authentication, and destination controls.

output_examples.input: Design events for a subscription checkout.
output: Plan Selected records the selected plan, billing interval, and source.
Checkout Started records the checkout identifier, amount, and currency.
Subscription Started records the subscription identifier, plan, amount, and interval.

output_examples.input: Review identity handling for a shared browser.
output_examples.output: Identify the user after authentication, preserve anonymous history during the merge, and reset Analytics.js during logout to prevent cross-user attribution.

output_examples.input: Limit personal data to trusted destinations.
output_examples.output: Disable all destinations by default for identity calls, then enable only approved CRM and warehouse destinations that meet the data policy.

best_practices: Use static Object Action event names and place changing values in properties.
Define required properties and types in a tracking plan before implementation.
Gate tracking on consent and restrict personal data to approved destinations.
anti_patterns: Do not build event names from user values or product identifiers.
Do not accept webhook or edge tracking requests without verification and validation.
Do not send personal data to every destination by default.

faq.question: Does this skill support browser and server tracking?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Analytics.js, the Node.js SDK, direct HTTP requests, and edge environments.

faq.question: Can it create a Segment tracking plan?
faq.answer: It can draft event schemas, required properties, types, and naming conventions for review and implementation.

faq.question: Does it configure my Segment workspace?
faq.answer: No. Workspace sources, destinations, and Protocols settings still require configuration through Segment tools.

faq.question: How does it handle user identity?
faq.answer: It explains anonymous IDs, identify calls, aliases, group calls, and logout reset requirements.

faq.question: Does it provide consent management?
faq.answer: No. It identifies consent as required, but the application must integrate and enforce an appropriate consent system.

faq.question: Are the examples ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Add authentication, validation, signature checks, rate limits, error handling, privacy controls, and environment-specific tests.
